Key capabilities I need implemented: • Automated outbound call scheduling with retry logic and time-zone awareness. • Real-time voice recognition powered by Natural Language Processing so the caller can respond naturally rather than keying in touch-tones. • A lightweight analytics layer that aggregates results and exposes them through a simple web dashboard plus downloadable CSV/JSON exports. I expect the stack to be Python-centric—FastAPI or Django for the service layer, a PostgreSQL or similar store for call and response data, and a telephony gateway such as Twilio, Plivo or Asterisk for call handling. items.description: ## Project Overview & Objectives We are seeking a developer to build a custom, multi-tenant Learning Management System (LMS) tailored for commercial fleet compliance and driver training. The system will replace standard video files with an interactive, slide-based presentation player utilizing synchronized background audio narration. The application should be built using a modern, scalable tech stack (freelancers are encouraged to propose their preferred backend and frontend frameworks), designed for optimal deployment on a standard Linux VPS environment. ## Core User Roles * **Super Admin:** Full platform control, interactive module creation, system-wide analytics, and company/tenant onboarding. * **Company Manager (Tenant):** Dashboard access to enroll their specific fleet drivers, track group compliance progress, and download completion reports. * **Driver (Learner):** Simplified frontend portal to access assigned modules, navigate slide-based presentations, take end-of-course assessments, and download earned certificates. ## Module & Feature Breakdown * **Multi-Tenant Organization Matrix:** Database architecture must support grouping users by distinct companies or branches to ensure isolated reporting and restricted manager access. * **Interactive Course Player Engine:** A custom media player that renders JSON-structured slides containing text, images, and pre-recorded audio instead of loading monolithic video streams. * **Enforced Progression Gating:** Slide navigation must be locked using mandatory timers or audio-duration listeners to ensure users cannot skip mandatory training materials. * **Assessment & Certification System:** Server-side evaluation of multiple-choice quizzes that triggers dynamic, downloadable PDF certificate generation upon achieving a passing score. * **Real-Time Compliance Dashboard:** A reporting data grid tracking individual enrollment statuses, start dates, last visited timestamps, final scores, and module statuses (Passed, Failed, Incomplete). ## Technical & Delivery Requirements * **Security & Access Control:** Secure authentication with custom username provisioning, strict role-based access control, and robust session management. * **State Management:** Relational database schema tracking user progress at the slide level to allow drivers to resume incomplete modules exactly where they left off. * **Deliverables:** Fully documented source code, complete database migration scripts, and an intuitive administrative interface

items.description: I’m looking for a programmer who can build a desktop application that automatically streams and completes around 1,000 video ads every day and performs a single extra action—clicking on each ad once it appears. My main requirement is that everything runs on a desktop environment, but if you already have (or can easily port) an Android build, let me know; Android would be the natural mobile extension for me later on. Here’s what success looks like for this first release: • The app launches on Windows or cross-platform runtimes (Electron, Python + Selenium, or any framework you prefer), opens the ad source in a browser instance or embedded player, watches the full ad without being flagged, and registers one click on the associated call-to-action. • It cycles through roughly 1,000 ads inside a 24-hour window without manual input, queueing the next video as soon as the previous one and its click are logged. • A simple dashboard or log file confirms how many ads were viewed and clicked, with timestamps for verification. • I can configure basic parameters myself (number of ads per session, delay between clicks, user-agent string, etc.) without touching code. Send me a brief outline of the tech stack you’ll use, how you’ll avoid detection, and an estimate of turnaround time. Once I see a solid proof of concept running through at least 100 ads without issues, we’ll move on to full-scale deployment and—if it makes sense—an Android companion.

New Lead Detection -Start the lead qualification workflow only when both conditions are met: The WhatsApp number is not saved as a contact in our WhatsApp Business account; and We have never previously received a message from that WhatsApp number. Tech requirements You are free to use Python, Node.js, or another language you’re comfortable with, as long as it integrates cleanly with the official WhatsApp Business Cloud API or a compliant provider such as Twilio. Replies must be text-only—no emojis, no links. Keyword–reply pairs should be editable in a simple JSON/CSV file or lightweight web dashboard that I can update without touching code. Deliverables 1. README showing how to add or change keywords and their fixed responses. Acceptance test I spin up the script, send a WhatsApp message containing a tracked keyword from another number, and receive the correct fixed text reply in under two seconds.

Core flow • Ingest live video streams from public surveillance cameras, run computer-vision models to spot floods, fires, crashes, or illegal dumping, and flag possible duplicates in real time. • Score every incident for risk and severity, then plot it instantly on an interactive map so dispatchers can see what matters first. • Suggest the most appropriate emergency response team automatically. • Notify citizens through SMS and in-app push notifications the moment an event affects their vicinity. • Give city managers an admin dashboard where they can filter, search, and export incident data. Python FastAPI services that: • accept camera feeds, run the initial incident-detection model (images and text), and log results to PostgreSQL; • expose endpoints for the live map, duplicate checking, scoring, and notification triggers. 3. Simple yet clean PostgreSQL schema covering incidents, media assets, users, and notifications. 4. Integrated Twilio or similar gateway for SMS, plus FCM/APNs for push. 5. Dockerised dev/prod setup and a basic CI pipeline so the city can deploy on its own infrastructure. Acceptance criteria • A demo city dashboard showing at least three simultaneously detected event types with correct scoring and mapping. • Citizens can register, receive an SMS and a push test alert, and acknowledge it. • Duplicate detection suppresses repeated camera frames with >90 % visual similarity. • Full repository, setup scripts, and README delivered. The first thing I do on every audit is look at the live app from the outside, the way a stranger would, before I open the editor. It runs: OWASP ZAP , crawling the live app and flagging security flaws in every page and response Nuclei , checking known vulnerabilities and misconfigurations for your stack, with templates updated daily Leaked keys : everything the browser downloads is scanned against 31 key patterns (Stripe, OpenAI, SendGrid, AWS and more). Useful if an API Connector key ever got left non-private. Vulnerable JavaScript libraries , including ones pulled in by plugins Email deliverability : SPF, DKIM and DMARC on your custom domain, so sign-up and reset emails don’t land in spam Lookalike domains that could be used to phish your users, plus forgotten subdomains found in public certificate logs Security headers, TLS, bot protection on your forms, broken links, mobile layout, accessibility, cookie consent and SEO What it doesn’t do: it doesn’t log in, and it doesn’t check your privacy rules or the Data API. That still needs someone inside the editor. Think of it as the outside-in half of an audit. The score is free, with no sign-up. The full report is $49 one time: every finding with evidence of where it was found, and the fix. If nothing Critical or Important turns up, you get a refund. LaunchProof Find out what your AI-built site leaks before your customers do Free score and verdict in four minutes: leaked keys, open databases, email delivery, accessibility and speed, with the exact fix for each.
